title: 哈姆雷特 3-4 寢宮驚變
style_suffix: black and white ink comic style, high contrast, heavy shadows, cold gothic atmosphere
characters: Hamlet, a lean young prince dressed head to toe in black, a short dark cloak, tousled dark hair, pale clean-shaven face with shadowed sleepless eyes

panels.prompt: the queen's candlelit bedchamber with a great curtained bed and a heavy woven arras along one wall, Polonius, a stooped elderly councillor with a long forked white beard, a heavy chain of office over dark robes, a rolled parchment in his sash, lifting the edge of the arras to slip behind it

dialogue.speaker: 波隆尼
dialogue.text: 他來了。請您狠狠教訓他——我就躲在這裡。
dialogue.en: He will come straight. Look you lay home to him... I'll sconce me even here. Pray you, be round with him.

panels.prompt: {characters} throwing open the chamber door, Queen Gertrude, a stately middle-aged queen with coiled auburn braids under a golden circlet, in a layered brocade gown, rising from her chair with brittle authority

dialogue.speaker: 葛簇特
dialogue.text: 哈姆雷特，你把你的父親大大得罪了。
dialogue.en: Hamlet, thou hast thy father much offended.

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 母親，你把我的父親大大得罪了。
dialogue.en: Mother, you have my father much offended.

panels.prompt: {characters} gripping his mother's wrist and forcing her down into the chair, her free hand flung up in fright, candle flames shuddering

dialogue.speaker: 葛簇特
dialogue.text: 你要幹什麼？你不是要殺我吧？——救命！救命啊！
dialogue.en: What wilt thou do? thou wilt not murder me? Help, help, ho!

panels.prompt: {characters} whirling and driving his sword clean through the bulging arras, the fabric caving around the blade, a muffled cry behind it

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.en: How now! a rat? Dead, for a ducat, dead!

quote.en: How now! a rat? Dead, for a ducat, dead!

panels.prompt: the arras pulled back to reveal Polonius, a stooped elderly councillor with a long forked white beard, a heavy chain of office over dark robes, a rolled parchment in his sash, crumpled dead against the wall, the queen's hands pressed to her mouth

dialogue.speaker: 葛簇特
dialogue.text: 啊，多麼鹵莽殘酷的行為！
dialogue.en: O me, what hast thou done?... O, what a rash and bloody deed is this!

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 殘酷的行為？好媽媽——跟殺了一個國王、再嫁給他的兄弟，差不多同樣壞。
dialogue.en: A bloody deed! almost as bad, good mother, as kill a king, and marry with his brother.

panels.prompt: {characters} looking down at the dead councillor with a weary, almost gentle contempt, sword point lowered to the floor

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 你這倒楣的、鹵莽的、愛管閒事的傻瓜，再會！我還以為是一個在你上面的人。
dialogue.en: Thou wretched, rash, intruding fool, farewell! I took thee for thy better.

panels.prompt: {characters} thrusting two miniature portrait lockets side by side before his mother's face, she twisting away, candlelight hard on the two tiny painted faces

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 瞧這一幅畫像，再瞧這一幅。這是你的前夫，額角上帶著天神的威嚴；這是你的現任丈夫——像一株霉爛的禾穗。你有眼睛嗎？
dialogue.en: Look here, upon this picture, and on this... See, what a grace was seated on this brow... Here is your husband; like a mildew'd ear... Have you eyes?

panels.prompt: Queen Gertrude, a stately middle-aged queen with coiled auburn braids under a golden circlet, in a layered brocade gown collapsed forward at her candlelit dressing table, face buried in her hands, the golden circlet slipped off among scattered pearls, the two miniature portrait lockets lying face-up between her elbows

dialogue.speaker: 葛簇特
dialogue.text: 啊，哈姆雷特，別說下去了！你使我的眼睛看進了我自己的靈魂——那上面的黑點，洗都洗不掉。
dialogue.en: O Hamlet, speak no more: thou turn'st mine eyes into my very soul; and there I see such black and grained spots as will not leave their tinct.

panels.prompt: a cold blue glow spilling from between the parted bed curtains, washing over Hamlet, a lean young prince dressed head to toe in black, a short dark cloak, tousled dark hair, pale clean-shaven face with shadowed sleepless eyes, dropped to his knees staring up into the light, while his mother shrinks back in her chair staring only at her kneeling son

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 天使保佑我！……您是來責備您兒子的拖延嗎？
dialogue.en: Save me, and hover o'er me with your wings, you heavenly guards!... Do you not come your tardy son to chide?

dialogue.speaker: 鬼魂
dialogue.text: 別忘記。我來，是要磨快你快要鈍了的決心。可是瞧——你的母親多麼驚恐，替她分憂吧。
dialogue.en: Do not forget: this visitation is but to whet thy almost blunted purpose. But, look, amazement on thy mother sits... speak to her, Hamlet.

panels.prompt: reverse angle: the bed curtains empty of any ghost, only shadow — Queen Gertrude clutching her son's arm, her eyes wide at the vacant air he stares into

dialogue.speaker: 葛簇特
dialogue.text: 唉，他瘋了——對著空氣說話。你在跟誰說話？我什麼也沒看見。
dialogue.en: Alas, he's mad!... To whom do you speak this?... Nothing at all; yet all that is I see.

panels.prompt: {characters} kneeling at his seated mother's side now gentle, taking her hands in both of his, the candles burned low around them

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 母親——向上天懺悔過去，警戒未來。不要上我叔父的床。今晚忍一忍，下一次就容易一些。
dialogue.en: Confess yourself to heaven; repent what's past; avoid what is to come... Go not to mine uncle's bed... Refrain to-night, and that shall lend a kind of easiness to the next abstinence.

panels.prompt: close two-shot, the queen's tear-streaked face against her son's, her circlet fallen to her lap

dialogue.speaker: 葛簇特
dialogue.text: 啊，哈姆雷特，你把我的心劈成兩半了。
dialogue.en: O Hamlet, thou hast cleft my heart in twain.

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 那就把壞的一半丟掉，用另外一半好好過活吧。
dialogue.en: O, throw away the worser part of it, and live the purer with the other half.

quote.text: 你把我的心劈成兩半了
quote.en: Thou hast cleft my heart in twain.

panels.prompt: very wide shot of the dim bedchamber doorway, {characters} dragging the heavy body of the old councillor out by the heels into the dark corridor, looking back over his shoulder one last time, a single guttering candle and the slumped queen small in the background

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 我必須到英格蘭去，你知道嗎？……這位大臣生前是個嘮叨的傻瓜，現在倒是嚴肅沉默得很。——晚安，母親。
dialogue.en: I must to England; you know that?... This counsellor is now most still, most secret and most grave, who was in life a foolish prating knave. — Good night, mother.
